_note: Standalone model (Exide Industries Ltd = the lead-acid business), the basis the street uses for the core (MOFSL, ICICI Securities report standalone numbers). The lithium-ion subsidiary EESL, the HDFC Life stake and other investments are valued separately in the sum of the parts. FY26 base = Screener standalone (revenue Rs17,269 cr, EBITDA Rs1,946 cr, PAT Rs1,111 cr). One segment ('core') so that bull/bear deltas flow through the engine's SOTP scenarios. Core, HDFC Life and EESL values are computed in tools/authoring/EXIDEIND.ctx.js and written here by EXIDEIND.val.js.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries (standalone Exide)
segments._why: Revenue = sum of five business lines (assumptions.build, checked in EXIDEIND.ctx.js). FY27E +12.9%: Q1FY27 +17.6% (volume double digit in most lines, prices +4-6% YoY), a low Q2 base (Q2FY26 -2% after the GST washout), then a high auto-OEM base in H2 (management, 3-Aug-2026). FY28-29E ~9%: management's medium-term 'high single digit to early double digit' for the core (5-year CAGR 11% +/-1%, Q4FY26 call), replacement demand from the FY26-27 OEM surge (2.5-3 years later), solar and exports recovering; telecom and e-rickshaw keep shifting to lithium.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis): FY26 11.3%, Q1FY27 12.3% (seasonal peak: inverter season; Q2FY26 was 9.5%). FY27E 11.6%: input costs (rupee lead, sulphur up from Rs15 to Rs75/kg, polypropylene) are being passed on in steps; cost-excellence savings. FY28-29E 11.9-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth. Street: MOFSL 11.2%/12.0% FY27-28E, ICICI Securities 11.9%/12.4%.

_capexWhy: Management keeps ~Rs500 cr a year for the lead-acid business (debottlenecking, automation, brownfield 4W capacity; Q1FY27 call). FY26 capex ~Rs409 cr (MOFSL). Lithium-ion capex sits in EESL, funded by equity infusions (see build.eeslInfusion), not here.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs501 cr; Q1FY27 Rs118 cr (run-rate ~Rs475 cr as older assets reach full depreciation). 7.0% of average gross block gives FY27E ~Rs480 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
_treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's 'treasury' includes the HDFC Life stake (Rs5,140 cr at Mar-26 fair value) and the EESL investment at cost (Rs4,802 cr), which earn no interest. Treasury income is built on liquid funds only, in otherIncome.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built (EXIDEIND.ctx.js checks it): 7% on average liquid funds (cash Rs165 cr + liquid mutual funds Rs254 cr at Mar-26; FY26 treasury income Rs32 cr: mutual-fund gains Rs30.6 cr + interest Rs1.2 cr) after funding EESL infusions, + dividends on investments Rs21-23 cr (HDFC Life, Faering, LIC Housing: Rs18.5 cr in FY26; subsidiaries Rs2.0 cr) + guarantee commission from EESL Rs6 cr (FY26 Rs5.6 cr) + foreign-exchange gains Rs10 cr (FY26 Rs27.9 cr, FY25 Rs9.5 cr; not forecast at the FY26 level) + other Rs7 cr. FY26 (Screener) Rs82 cr; TTM to Jun-2026 Rs79 cr; Q1FY27 Rs14 cr as cash went to EESL.
_interestWhy: Standalone is debt-free; FY26 finance cost Rs34.9 cr of which lease interest Rs32.9 cr (AR FY26 note 30). Q1FY27 Rs8 cr.
_taxWhy: New regime (25.17%) plus small disallowances: FY26 effective 25.5%, Q1FY27 25.0%.
_payoutWhy: Rs2 per share for FY24-26 (FY26 dividend Rs170 cr proposed, AR FY26 note 16): 15% of FY26 EPS. Cash is being kept for the lithium-ion project.

build._why: Auto (OEM + replacement, domestic): OEM +25% for three quarters on the GST cut, 4W replacement volume +10% in Q1FY27; H2 base high. Home UPS/inverter (Rs2,300 cr, 15-25% of revenue by season): a strong summer in Q1FY27. Solar (crossed Rs1,000 cr in FY26; >Rs400 cr in Q1FY27). Exports (Rs915 cr, ~5%; down from ~8%): +20% in Q1FY27 off a low base. Industrial domestic: infrastructure ex-telecom double digit, government tenders soft until H2FY27, telecom (~2-3%) shrinking.
build._eeslInfusionWhy: FY27E: Board-approved Rs1,400 cr (Rs100 cr paid in July; capex plus operating and working-capital needs). FY28-29E: none in the core cash path. EESL losses after the target date are charged once, as a present value in the EESL line of the sum of the parts (PLAYBOOK §7c); Phase 2 (6 to 12 GWh) is not approved and is excluded.

eesl._lossWhy: GAM estimates (no company guidance; brokers do not publish EESL forecasts). FY26 loss Rs248 cr before commercial production (AOC-1); the consolidated-less-standalone gap was Rs56 cr in Q1FY27. From commercial start in FY27 depreciation on ~Rs4,500-5,000 cr of plant (~Rs300 cr a year) and interest on ~Rs1,200 cr of subsidiary borrowings (consolidated less standalone borrowings at Mar-26) arrive before volumes: management guides 25-30% utilisation of 6 GWh in the first year and 85% utilisation with 90% yield as the target. Base: breakeven in FY30E. Bull: FY30E with smaller losses (PLI-style support, Hyundai-Kia line). Bear: losses persist into FY30E, breakeven FY31E.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free consumer-and-industrial battery maker with lead-price pass-through: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%.
dcf._tgWhy: Batteries track vehicle parc, power back-up and industrial capex: ~5.5% nominal long-run growth (house range 5-6%), below India's ~10% nominal GDP as telecom and e-rickshaw move to lithium.
dcf._fadeWhy: Growth fades from ~9% to 7%; margin held at 12% (FY17-26 band 10.7-14.0%); capex 3% of sales (FY27-29E ~2.4-2.6% plus periodic capacity steps); depreciation 2.6% of sales.
dcf._netCashWhy: The engine adds 'treasury' at FY27E: liquid funds + the HDFC Life stake at Mar-26 fair value + EESL and other investments at cost. So the DCF is a core DCF plus those investments at book, a cross-check only.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The post-GST auto cycle and the replacement wave it creates lift volumes; solar and exports keep growing in double digits; price increases stick and margin reaches ~12.5%; EESL ramps faster (losses shrink, breakeven FY30E); HDFC Life valued near market.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Auto-OEM growth reverses against the high base, rupee lead and sulphur costs outrun price increases (margin back to ~11%), telecom and e-rickshaw shift to lithium faster; EESL yields and approvals lag (breakeven FY31E) and the market values the plant at half of book; HDFC Life at a 30% discount.

parts.name: Lead-acid core: P/E on Sep-28E standalone EPS (ex HDFC Life dividend)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E standalone EPS Rs19.6 less HDFC Life dividend Rs0.16 x 15.5x (bull 17x on Rs21.7, bear 10x on Rs16.5) x 85.00 cr shares
parts.note: Core P/E = Exide's own forward P/E net of its investments (median 17x since the Exide Life sale, Jan-2022 to Sep-2026) x the auto-component sector move (−7.8%), nearest half-turn.

parts.name: HDFC Life: 8.70 cr shares at market less discount
parts.metricLabel: 8.70 cr shares x Rs521.2 (NSE close, 30-Sep-2026) = Rs4,536 cr, less 20% (bull 10%, bear 30%)
parts.note: Discount = the one MOFSL applies (Rs45/share at the 31-Jul-2026 price of Rs548.5); shares unchanged since 1-Jan-2022 (AR FY26 note 4; HDFC Life Jun-2026 pattern).

parts.name: Exide Energy Solutions (lithium-ion): book less PV of losses to breakeven
parts.metricLabel: Book equity at Sep-27E Rs4,800 cr (Mar-26 Rs4,025 cr + FY27 infusion Rs1,400 cr − losses) x 1 less PV of losses to breakeven Rs337 cr (bear: 0.5x book)
parts.note: GAM loss path FY27-30E Rs450/350/190/0 cr (bull 400/220/60/0, bear 550/500/350/150), discounted at 12.5% (PLAYBOOK §7c: present value of losses to breakeven).

parts.name: Other investments and subsidiaries at book
parts.metricLabel: Mar-26 carrying value: Chloride Metals and other subsidiaries, Faering fund, unquoted stakes (AR FY26 note 4)
parts.note: Chloride Metals (lead recycling, 100%) lost Rs14 cr in FY26; book value used.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Exide: P/E on the standalone lead-acid EPS plus the lithium-ion plant at book or invested capital plus the HDFC Life stake (MOFSL, ICICI Securities).

methods.name: P/E on standalone EPS
methods.why: The core multiple applied to all standalone EPS, with EESL and HDFC Life left out: shows what the parts add.

methods.name: DCF (core + investments at book)
methods.why: Ten-year FCFF of the standalone business at a 12.5% cost of equity, plus liquid funds, HDFC Life at Mar-26 fair value and EESL at cost.
